package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions distributed via malicious gaming apps)
package_info.why_malicious: Electron-bot is a malware family distributed through trojanized gaming applications on the Microsoft Store. It covertly hijacks victims' social media accounts by automating browser sessions to log in with stolen credentials, performs unauthorized actions such as liking, commenting, following, and registering new accounts, and enables remote attackers to control the victim's social media presence. These behaviors are not expected in legitimate gaming applications and represent credential theft, account abuse, and potential further propagation.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user launches the gaming application)
execution_context.file_location: main application code (JavaScript/Node.js within Electron app, typically in main.js or a similar entry point)
required_permissions: network access (to communicate with social media and C2 servers)
browser automation (to control headless browser sessions)
access to stored social media credentials

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (after the user launches the gaming application), the code uses Puppeteer to launch a headless browser, navigates to social media login pages, inputs stored or stolen user credentials, and automates actions such as liking, commenting, and registering new accounts. The data flow involves reading credentials, automating browser actions, and sending engagement data to remote servers, resulting in unauthorized remote control and abuse of the victim's social media accounts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of browser automation to log in to social media accounts and perform engagement actions from a gaming application is highly suspicious, as it indicates credential harvesting and remote command execution unrelated to the app's stated purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate gaming applications should not automate browser sessions to log in to social media accounts, nor should they perform actions on behalf of the user without explicit consent. Such automation is not required for normal game functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Browser automation libraries like Puppeteer are legitimately used in software testing and QA environments, but their presence and use in consumer-facing gaming apps is highly anomalous and indicative of malicious intent.
key_indicators: Inclusion and use of Puppeteer or similar browser automation libraries in a gaming app
Automated login attempts to social media platforms using user credentials
Execution of social media engagement actions (like, comment, follow) via automated scripts
Network communication with remote servers to receive commands or exfiltrate engagement data

attack_chain.action: User installs a trojanized gaming application from the Microsoft Store that contains Electron-bot malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present on the victim's system and awaits execution.

attack_chain.action: When the user launches the gaming application, the malware executes browser automation code to log in to the victim's social media accounts using stored or stolen credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Automated access to social media accounts and initiation of unauthorized actions.

attack_chain.action: The malware performs automated actions such as registering new accounts, liking, commenting, and following, all under remote attacker control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Abuse of the victim's social media presence, potential further propagation, and possible monetization through fake engagement.

behavioral_signatures: Gaming applications invoking browser automation libraries (e.g., Puppeteer, Selenium) at runtime
Automated login attempts to social media sites (e.g., facebook.com, google.com, soundcloud.com) from non-browser processes
Unusual network traffic to social media APIs or endpoints originating from gaming app processes
Gaming app processes spawning headless browser instances
file_indicators: Presence of Puppeteer or similar browser automation modules in the application package (e.g., node_modules/puppeteer/)
Unexpected JavaScript files containing browser automation logic in Electron app directories (e.g., main.js, automation.js)
Gaming app package containing configuration files or scripts referencing social media login URLs
network_indicators: Outbound connections to social media login endpoints (e.g., https://facebook.com/login, https://accounts.google.com/signin) from gaming app processes
Connections to remote command and control (C2) servers for receiving automation instructions (domains/IPs as identified in threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual POST or GET requests to social media APIs from non-browser user agents
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor gaming applications for the presence and invocation of browser automation libraries such as Puppeteer or Selenium. Flag applications that initiate automated login or engagement actions on social media platforms from non-browser processes. Inspect application packages for the inclusion of browser automation modules and scripts referencing social media endpoints. Correlate with network telemetry to identify outbound connections to social media login pages or C2 servers, and investigate user reports of unauthorized social media activity originating from gaming apps.
